context.text: john cabot is a person. John Cabot's 1497 voyage was to the coast of North America. An Italian navigator and explorer born in Italy, known as Giovanni Caboto in Italian, Zuan Caboto in Venetian, Jean Cabot in French, and John Cabot in English. He was the son of Giulio Caboto and his wife, and had a brother named Piero. In 1476, he became a citizen of the Republic of Venice after living there since at least 1461. He was accepted into the Scuola Grande di San Giovanni Evangelista in 1471. Cabot engaged in Mediterranean trade, including selling a slave acquired in the territories of the Sultan of Egypt. After facing financial trouble and becoming an insolvent debtor in Venice in 1488, he moved to Valencia, Spain, where he proposed harbor improvements. He later worked on a stone bridge over the Guadalquivir river in Seville before seeking support for an Atlantic expedition in Seville and Lisbon. In mid-1495, he reached England to seek funding and political support from Henry VII of England. He received a royal patent in 1496 to explore the eastern, western, and northern seas. Cabot made a first voyage in the summer of 1496 with one ship. His second voyage took place in 1497 on the Matthew of Bristol, making landfall on the coast of North America on 24 June 1497.
